subject: Clarify DPA incident notification: scope, timelines, and cross-border evidence routing

Subject: DPA: incident notification wording and evidence transfer questions

Hi Grace,

Thanks for your time last week. Our legal and security teams started reviewing the DPA and we have a few follow-ups specific to incident notification and cross-border evidence handling that we need to resolve before procurement can sign. High level items:

- Timeline: Our procurement counsel is pushing for "customer notification within 48 hours of discovery" for any incident affecting personal data. We see Redwood's standard varies in your docs (48/72h), can you confirm the definitive timeline you can commit to in an EU contract?
- Scope: We need explicit language that clarifies whether incidents impacting metadata (IP, device identifiers, usage telemetry) count as "personal data incidents" for the purposes of the window.
- Subprocessors: If a subprocessor is implicated, will Redwood notify us proactively and share the subprocessor remediation plan and contact?
- Evidence & transfers: For cross-border forensic exports, do you require a separate legal request/MLAT-style agreement? What redaction/minimisation controls will you apply before transferring raw logs?

Can you point us to an internal contact to work through a short mutual action plan (timeline + sample exported artifacts)? Ideally we want to lock text this week so legal can move to signature.

Appreciate a quick reply—cc'ing security@finstratech.com for any technical follow-ups.

Best,

Hi Liz — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Kim (legal) and Ben (security operations) to confirm details but wanted to give you our practical position upfront so procurement/legal have something to work with.

Summary of Redwood's standard (proposed contract language we typically accept):
- Initial notice: Redwood will provide an initial customer notification "as soon as reasonably practicable" after confirmation that an incident has affected Customer Personal Data, and in any event no later than 72 hours from confirmation of the incident. For high-confidence incidents where we can confidently identify impacted customer records within 24–48 hours, we will aim to send a preliminary notification within 48 hours.
- Scope: We treat any data that falls under your contract's definition of Personal Data as in-scope. That includes identifiers and device-level telemetry when they meet the legal threshold for personal data under applicable law. Aggregated or fully anonymized telemetry is excluded.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will notify the Customer of any implicated subprocessor(s) within the initial notification and will share the subprocessor's remediation summary and primary contact within 48 hours of Redwood's confirmation of impact.
- Evidence & transfers: Redwood can provide forensic artifacts (logs, packet captures, snapshots) under a limited-scope evidence transfer process. For cross-border moves we require either (a) an executed MOU/forensics transfer agreement referencing lawful bases for transfer and data minimisation rules, or (b) a lawful request from an authorized Customer representative that includes a data minimisation manifest. Where feasible we will provide pseudonymized extracts or hashed digests before full exports.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to run a quick internal mapping of what exports we can produce within 48 hours vs what needs a formal forensic export process.
2) Kim to draft a short MOU template that lays out the transfer controls and retention/destruction obligations.
3) I can send a proposed paragraph for your DPA that reflects the 72-hour baseline with a 48-hour best-effort preliminary notice.

Attached: Draft_Redwood_MOU_for_Forensics.pdf (playbook + minimum manifest), forensic_export_manifest_template.xlsx

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call today or tomorrow to walk through — what time slot works?

Best,

Grace / Liz — I've reviewed the proposed position and attached a short redline with a few constraints we should keep in the commercial DPA. Key points: 

1) Timing carve: we should avoid an absolute 48-hour contracted deadline for all "incidents". I suggest contract language along the lines of: "Redwood will provide notice to Customer as soon as reasonably practicable and, with respect to confirmed incidents affecting Customer Personal Data, no later than seventy-two (72) hours after confirmation of such incident, except where legal/regulatory obligations or ongoing criminal investigations prevent disclosure." This gives us flexibility if law enforcement asks us to postpone.

2) Scope clarification: define "Personal Data" by reference to the DPA's definition and include an explicit list (e.g., identifiers, device ids, user-provided content) to avoid surprises. We can offer a non-binding mapping appendix showing how common telemetry fields are classified.

3) Evidence transfer controls: we can offer pseudonymized telemetry and digests by default. Full raw exports should require: a) a Customer-authorized request signed by an authorized legal contact, b) a minimal manifest describing the precise fields/time windows, and c) assurances on onward transfer controls if crossing jurisdictions. If FinStratech needs an operational path for emergency law-enforcement-driven export, that should go through a separate SLA & fee schedule.

4) Subprocessor notice: we can commit to notifying impacted subprocessors in the initial notice and provide contact + remediation plan within 48 hours of confirmation of impact, unless the subprocessor's own restrictions prevent sharing (in which case we'll summarize).

I've attached redlines to the DPA and a draft of the minimal forensic manifest (redlines_dpa_notify_clause.docx). Ben, please add a note on what we can reliably produce within 48 hours vs what takes 5–10 business days.

-Kim

(Attachment: redlines_dpa_notify_clause.docx)

Hi all — quick wrap with concrete language we can propose to procurement today.

Proposed DPA paragraph (suggested):
"In the event of an incident that Redwood reasonably determines has resulted in the unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Personal Data, Redwood will: (a) provide initial notice to Customer as soon as reasonably practicable and no later than seventy-two (72) hours after Redwood's confirmation that Customer Personal Data has been affected (subject to lawful restrictions and ongoing criminal investigations); (b) in the initial notice, identify any implicated Redwood subprocessors; and (c) within forty-eight (48) hours of confirmation, use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a remediation summary and subprocessor contact details. Redwood will make available forensic artifacts subject to a limited-scope evidence transfer process that requires an authorized Customer request and a data minimisation manifest; where cross-border transfer is necessary Redwood will apply pseudonymisation and minimisation, and where required by law will seek a mutually executed forensics transfer MOU prior to transfer."

Operational commitments:
- Within 48 hours we can reliably deliver: event timelines, impacted subsystem identifiers, redacted log extracts (pseudonymised), and a subprocessor remediation summary.
- Full raw exports (pcaps, full request/response payloads) typically require completion of the forensics MOU and can take 3–10 business days depending on scope and export authorisation.
- For urgent law-enforcement requests we will coordinate through an agreed escalation channel; we may pause customer notice at the request of law enforcement and will notify the Customer when and if notice is permissible.

If that language aligns with FinStratech's needs, I'm happy to send over the DPA paragraph as tracked changes and we can schedule a 30-minute call to finalize. Proposed slots: tomorrow 09:00–10:00 or 15:00–15:30 CET.

Thanks,
Grace
